newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Armani may tread flotation catwalk.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Armani may tread flotation catwalk.

text.p: Italian designer Giorgio Armani is giving his fashion empire a makeover in order to simplify its retail operations, sparking speculation Tuesday that Italy's best-selling stylist is considering taking his business public.
A statement from Giorgio Armani Spa said it had restructured its retail operations and had embarked on a project which could lead to the spinoff of its financial and design units.
Armani's move comes after rival Milan fashion designers including Gianni Versace Spa, whose founder was shot dead in July, are already getting in shape for a planned sale to investors next year.
The statement made no mention of a possible flotation but newspapers and equity analysts speculated the announcement could herald preparations for a stock market listing.
"It's probable that this restructuring is leading up to a stock market listing," said Lorenzo Iori, a fashion industry analyst at Milan brokerage Murchio & Co.

Analysts said a stock offering from Armani would be as attractive as one of his fashionable suits. "An Armani public offer would be very interesting for investors looking to buy 'made in Italy,'" said Angelo Di Cresce, head of sales at brokers InterSIM.
"Fashion has better international appeal than, say, disc brakes or machine tools," he added.
Armani, who dresses film and rock stars, said earlier this year a listing could be one route to consider for the future.
He has built up his exclusive ready-to-wear lines and accessories since founding Giorgio Armani SpA in 1975.
Now he has re-designed his retail network, comprising 59 Boutiques Giorgio Armani and 133 Emporio Armani stores worldwide, into a simpler structure.

Early next year, domestic Italian retail operations for both the eight Boutiques and the 53 stores in the lower-priced Emporio Armani line will be handled by a new company called S. Andrea Srl. Foreign retail operations will remain separate.
Along with overhauling his retail division, Armani also has plans for a possible spinoff of the financial and design units of Giorgio Armani SpA, the designer's holding company.

Ultimately Giorgio Armani SpA would control the designer's retailing operations through S. Andrea, along with 53 percent of listed apparel maker Simint SpA. The newly spun off design and financial arms would be owned directly by Armani himself.

Analysts say the complex structure of Italian fashion houses makes them difficult to sell to investors unless they are reorganized first. Many outsource production to smaller companies, and handle only the design and licensing themselves.
Armani's production is split between four companies.
"It looks like Armani's strategy is to bring production slowly under one umbrella as his various production contracts expire, and then sell part of that company," Iori said.
"A company including about half of his stores and a fraction of his production is not really representative of his business."
The holding company expects sales from clothing, perfumes and accessories to reach a consolidated 1.35 trillion lire ($755 million) this year, making it Italy's top-selling fashion house.
No one was available for further comment at Armani's Milan press office.
Italian designers have shown growing interest recently in offering their private empires to the public, following the successful flotation in 1995 of luxury goods group Gucci.
Plans to sell part of Gianni Versace SpA next spring on the New York and Milan exchanges continue despite the designer's recent death in a shooting outside his Miami villa.
